fullPassage: The act of improvisation, when it enters our thoughts, is generally contextualized within the realm of the arts. A group of jazz musicians gather without any sheet music and invent music that’s never been heard before, and actors venture onto stages or in front of cameras and perform scenes without a script, making up the dialogue and actions on the spot. In both cases, each set of performers finds artistic success ―they entertain their audiences through improvisation, by creating something new in the moment. However, this skill is not confined to artistic endeavors; it proves equally useful in negotiations, where, for negotiators, there is no script —only a stage. Negotiators can’t plan for all the possible directions a negotiation might take, nor can they predict the changing demands of the other party. Improvisation empowers them to think on their feet and thrive in fluctuating circumstances so that they can maintain a position of strength throughout the negotiation process. To improvise effectively, negotiators, like musicians and actors, must actively listen. The ability to listen is what allows a negotiator to identify the interests of the other party and respond appropriately to work toward a mutually beneficial resolution. Attentive listening also builds trust and encourages sincere participation from everyone involved. It shows the other party that the negotiator is willing to cooperate in helping them achieve their objectives rather than trying to just dominate the negotiation. Employing improvisation instead of a set pattern of reasoning further frees the mind to pursue divergent thinking, which can help negotiators come up with out-of-the-box solutions that otherwise would not be available.

② no reward(보상 없음) — 계획 불가 흐름과 연결되지 않음
③ no audience(관객 없음) — 협상의 즉흥성과 무관
④ no deadline(마감 없음) — 대본·무대 비유와 어긋남
det.tip: there is ____ —only a stage → 대본은 없고 무대만 → no script

questions.passage: The act of improvisation, when it enters our thoughts, is generally contextualized within the realm of the arts. A group of jazz musicians gather without any sheet music and invent music that’s never been heard before, and actors venture onto stages or in front of cameras and perform scenes without a script, making up the dialogue and actions on the spot. In both cases, each set of performers finds artistic success ―they entertain their audiences through improvisation, by creating something new in the moment. However, this skill is not confined to artistic endeavors; it proves equally useful in negotiations, where, for negotiators, there is no script —only a stage. Negotiators can’t plan for all the possible directions a negotiation might take, nor can they predict the changing demands of the other party. Improvisation empowers them to think on their feet and thrive in fluctuating circumstances so that they can __________ throughout the negotiation process. To improvise effectively, negotiators, like musicians and actors, must actively listen. The ability to listen is what allows a negotiator to identify the interests of the other party and respond appropriately to work toward a mutually beneficial resolution. Attentive listening also builds trust and encourages sincere participation from everyone involved. It shows the other party that the negotiator is willing to cooperate in helping them achieve their objectives rather than trying to just dominate the negotiation. Employing improvisation instead of a set pattern of reasoning further frees the mind to pursue divergent thinking, which can help negotiators come up with out-of-the-box solutions that otherwise would not be available.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: maintain a position of strength=우위를 유지하다
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞은 '즉흥이 즉석 대처하고 변동하는 상황에서 잘 헤쳐 나가게 하여 협상 내내 ____ 하게 한다'는 흐름이므로, 강한 위치(우위)를 지킴을 뜻하는 maintain a position of strength가 적절
① avoid every difficult question(모든 어려운 질문을 피한다) — 적극적 대처 흐름과 반대
② maintain a position of strength(우위를 유지한다) ✅ 정답 — 협상 내내 강한 위치를 지킴
③ end the talks immediately(즉시 협상을 끝낸다) — 본문 취지와 무관
④ follow a fixed script(고정된 대본을 따른다) — 대본이 없다는 앞 내용과 모순
det.tip: thrive in fluctuating circumstances → 협상 내내 우위(strength)를 유지

det.korean: ① 경청 능력이 이해관계 파악·적절한 대응을 가능하게 한다 — 본문과 일치
det.analysis:
① 일치 — 'The ability to listen is what allows a negotiator to identify the interests of the other party and respond appropriately' ←정답
② 불일치 — 본문은 'willing to cooperate ... rather than trying to just dominate'로, 지배가 아니라 협력을 강조함

④ 불일치 — 'builds trust and encourages sincere participation'으로, 경청은 신뢰와 참여를 늘림
det.tip: identify the interests ... and respond appropriately = 이해관계 파악·대응

ch: 경청 능력은 상대의 이해관계를 파악하고 적절히 대응하게 해 준다.
협상가는 상대를 지배하는 것을 가장 중요한 목표로 삼아야 한다.
정해진 추론 방식을 따를 때 틀을 벗어난 해결책이 더 잘 나온다.
주의 깊은 경청은 오히려 신뢰를 무너뜨리고 참여를 줄인다.

questions.passage: To improvise effectively, negotiators must actively ①<u>listen</u> to the other party. The ability to listen ②<u>allow</u> a negotiator to identify the interests of the other party. Attentive listening also ③<u>builds</u> trust and encourages sincere participation. It shows the negotiator is willing ④<u>to cooperate</u> rather than to dominate.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② allow → allows: 주어 The ability가 단수이므로 단수동사 allows
det.analysis:
❌ ① listen — 'must actively listen(적극적으로 경청해야 한다)'으로 조동사 뒤 원형이라 올바릅니다.

✅ ② allow — 원래는 allows예요. 주어가 'The ability(능력)'로 단수예요. 중간에 'to listen'이 끼어 있어 헷갈리지만, 진짜 주어는 The ability라서 단수동사 allows로 써야 해요. ←정답

❌ ③ builds — 주어 'Attentive listening'이 단수라 단수동사 builds가 올바릅니다.

❌ ④ to cooperate — 'is willing to cooperate(기꺼이 협력하려 한다)'로 be willing to 구문이라 올바릅니다.
det.tip: 주어 The ability(단수) + 단수동사 allows. 사이에 낀 to listen에 속지 말기

questions.stem: 다음 설명에 해당하는 표현을 위 글의 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오: 즉흥이 협상가로 하여금 '즉석에서, 그 자리에서 재빨리' 판단하게 함을 나타내며, think 바로 뒤에 이어지는 표현. (영어로, 3단어)

questions.passage: It shows the other party that the negotiator is willing to cooperate in __________ (help) them achieve their objectives rather than trying to just dominate the negotiation.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 전치사 in 뒤에는 동명사가 오므로 help → helping
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞에 전치사 in(~하는 데)이 있어요. 전치사 뒤에는 동사를 그대로 쓸 수 없고 -ing(동명사)로 바꿔야 해요
그래서 help를 helping으로 써서 'in helping them(그들을 돕는 데)'이 돼요. 동사원형 help를 그대로 두면 전치사 뒤 형태가 틀려요
det.tip: 전치사(in, by, of 등) 뒤에는 동명사(-ing): help → helping

다음 우리말에 맞도록 [조건]에 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 알맞은 영어를 쓰시오. (영어로) 그 협상가가 기꺼이 협력하려 한다(는 것을 보여 준다). It shows the other party that ______________________ in helping them achieve their objectives. (6단어)
[조건] (1) cooperate, is, negotiator, the, to, willing 을 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 6단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 주어(the negotiator) + be동사(is) + willing to + 동사원형(cooperate)
det.analysis:
'그 협상가'는 the negotiator로 주어예요. '기꺼이 ~하려 한다'는 be willing to do 구문을 써요
주어가 단수(the negotiator)라 be동사는 is를 쓰고, willing 뒤에는 to + 동사원형이 오므로 to cooperate가 돼요
순서대로 이으면 the negotiator is willing to cooperate, 총 6단어예요
det.tip: be willing to + 동사원형 = 기꺼이 ~하려 하다 (the negotiator is willing to cooperate)

questions.wa: the negotiator is willing to cooperate
accept: the negotiator is willing to cooperate
